transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doc. Well, I guess what brought me in is that people just keep saying I’m not listening to them. 

My supervisor at work or my wife, they'll be talking straight to me, and... a minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I end up having to ask them to say it all over again. It's getting to be a real problem, so I figured I should come in.

When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting—like a hobby or watching something you like—do you have the same trouble focusing and listening, or does it seem to happen mainly in situations like work or conversations with your wife?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't... I haven't really thought about it like that. 

I mostly just notice it when I'm getting chewed out by my supervisor at the plant, or when my wife gets frustrated with me. If I'm doing something I actually like... I don't know. I guess I haven't really paid enough attention to whether it happens then too.
Going back to when you were younger—in school, for example—did teachers or your parents ever mention that you had trouble paying attention or focusing, even back then?

Yeah, I was actually like this even as a kid. Teachers were always moving my seat around because I just couldn’t stay put. I'd always be calling out answers in class, and... well, I got into a lot of trouble for butting into other kids’ work. That was all way back before middle school, mostly. So, yeah, they definitely brought it up back then.

When you're really into something you enjoy—like a hobby, a show you love, or a game—can you sit and focus on that for a long time without your mind wandering, or do you find yourself getting distracted and restless even then?

Honestly, Doc, it's kind of like what I was saying a minute ago... I really couldn't tell you. When I'm watching a game or messing around in the garage, I'm just not keeping track of whether my mind is wandering or if I'm getting restless. 

I just haven't paid attention to it. I only really notice there's a problem when somebody gets mad at me for it, like at work or at home. So, yeah, I'm just not sure how I am with the fun stuff.

When you're at work on a task that's routine or boring—something you don't particularly enjoy—can you stick with it and concentrate, or do you find yourself getting distracted and having trouble staying focused on that kind of work?

I'm really not sure about that, either. A lot of my job at the plant is pretty routine, but... I don't really track what my brain is doing while I'm working. 

I don't know if I'm losing focus or getting distracted just because the work is boring. Like I said, I mostly just know there's a problem when my supervisor gets on my case for something. I've never really stopped to think about whether I'm having trouble concentrating in those specific moments. I just go in and do my shift.

When you were a kid and teachers were moving your seat around—was that mainly because you couldn't sit still and were fidgeting and moving around, or was it more because you weren't paying attention to what was being taught?

It was definitely because I couldn't sit still. I was always moving. And honestly, it's still like that now. If I’m sitting in a safety huddle at the plant, or even just at the dinner table at home, my leg is always bouncing. My hands are always messing with a pen or jingling my keys... folks actually tell me I’m shaking the whole bench sometimes. So yeah, it was the fidgeting, for sure.

When you're in the garage doing something you really enjoy—like working on a project or tinkering with something—do people ever complain that you're not listening to them, or do they seem to get your attention pretty easily then?

Well, actually, that's kind of the main reason I'm here. People complain about me not listening all the time, no matter what I'm doing. 

Like, my supervisor at work or my wife at home, they'll be standing right in front of me, talking straight to my face. And... I don't know, a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I'm having to ask them to repeat the whole thing. It happens when I'm in the garage, too. My wife will come out to tell me something while I'm tinkering, and I just... I miss it.

When you're working on something in the garage that you really enjoy—like a project you're genuinely interested in—and someone tries to talk to you, do you miss what they're saying just as often as you do at work or at the dinner table, or do you actually catch what they say more easily then?

I honestly couldn't tell you if there's a difference. I mean, I know I miss things she says when I'm out there working on a project, but... I've never really paid attention to whether it happens exactly as often as it does at work or at the table. 

I just know it happens enough that people get annoyed with me pretty much everywhere. I haven't really noticed if being interested in what I'm doing makes me hear them any better or worse.

Let me ask this a different way: When you're doing something in the garage that you're really into—like a project you actually care about—and nobody is trying to talk to you, can you work on that for hours without feeling like you need to get up and do something else, or do you find yourself getting restless and wanting to move on to something different even when you're enjoying it?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. When I'm out there working on something, I'm usually moving around anyway—walking over to the toolbox, grabbing a wrench, checking on something else. 

So... I don't know if I ever just stand in one spot for hours on one single thing. I've never really kept track of whether I'm getting restless with the actual project and wanting to quit, or if I'm just naturally moving around like I always do. I just haven't paid that close attention to it.

You mentioned your leg bounces and your hands are always fidgeting—like with a pen or your keys. Does that happen pretty much all day long, even when you're trying to relax or sit still, or is it mainly when you're at work or in situations where you have to sit through something?

Well, it's pretty much anytime I have to sit, really. Like, if I’m sitting in a safety huddle at work, or even just at the dinner table at home... my leg is always bouncing. My hands are just naturally messing with a pen or my keys. It's bad enough that folks will actually tell me I’m shaking the whole bench. So yeah, it happens a lot, not just when I'm on the clock.

When you're doing something you really enjoy in the garage—something you're genuinely interested in and care about—and you're working on it alone without anyone bothering you, can you tell me: do you lose track of time and find yourself working on that one project for a long stretch, or do you tend to bounce around from one thing to another even though you're enjoying it?

I honestly don't know. Like I said before, I'm always moving around out there anyway, so it's hard to tell if I'm bouncing from one thing to another or just working on different parts of the same project. I don't really keep track of the time or how long I stay on one specific task. I just go out there and do what needs doing until I'm done or have to come back inside. I haven't ever stopped to think about if I'm losing track of time or jumping around.
